content.text:
Use compaction when the session is still on the same goal but the context is getting noisy. After compaction, ask Claude to restate: Restate the goal, files changed, remaining tasks, and verification commands.

When a Claude Code session gets long enough that nobody can remember which decision mattered, compaction starts to look attractive. It summarizes the session so work can continue with less context. That helps, but it is still compression. Details can be lost. Before a long task compacts, make sure the important state is in the filesystem: The plan is written in a file or reflected in tests. The branch diff is coherent. Verification commands are known. Blockers are documented with command output. Decisions are captured in CLAUDE.md, rules, skills, or project documentation when they need to persist. If a future session needs to remember a subtle decision, put that decision in a file before compaction. 

Use compaction when the session is still on the same goal but the context is getting noisy. After compaction, ask Claude to restate: Restate the goal, files changed, remaining tasks, and verification commands.

Claude Code exposes hook events around compaction. Use them sparingly for auditing or preserving status, not for hiding critical project state in an invisible automation. Large-context model aliases such as sonnet[1m] and opus[1m] can reduce the need to compact, but they do not remove the need for clean task state. A million tokens of unclear conversation is still unclear.

Use Claude Code compaction deliberately, preserve task state in files, and avoid relying on long chat history for correctness.

content.title: Claude Code Compaction: How Context Compression ...
content.text:
/compact summarizes older conversation messages and replaces the long transcript with shorter context. It does not reset the project or delete files; it changes what the active session can “remember” from earlier turns.

For the active model call, older messages are represented by a compact summary after the compaction boundary. In SDK workflows, treat compact_boundary and its metadata as a real context boundary: do not assume every pre-compact message is still available to the model verbatim. Claude Code runs in your terminal and maintains long sessions. Unlike ChatGPT where each message is a separate request, Claude Code accumulates context: files it read, commands it executed, grep results, diffs, error messages. All of this stacks into one massive prompt. The problem: models have context window limits. Claude Sonnet has 200K tokens, Opus goes up to 1M. But even a million tokens runs out when your agent is actively working through a codebase. 

Compaction kicks in when context reaches roughly 95% of the limit. What happens: Claude Code takes the entire conversation history, sends it to a separate model call with a prompt like "compress this into key facts," and replaces the full history with a condens

Claude Code /compact explained: what context automatically compacted means, what survives compression, compact prompts, hooks and how to recover lost context. When Claude Code reaches its context window limit, it compacts the conversation: older messages become a shorter summary so the session can continue. Project files stay unchanged, but details that only lived in chat can disappear from the active context. There's a hidden mechanic in Claude Code that most people don't think about until it costs them an hour of work. Compaction is the automatic compression of your conversation context when you approach the token limit. 

I ran into it when my always-on agent "forgot" a critical rule from the beginning of a session after 200 minutes of continuous operation.

content.title: Claude Code Compaction and Long-Session Operations Guide - Managing Context Across Long and Multi-Session Work | hidekazu-konishi.com
content.text:
/context visualizes current context usage as a colored grid, with a per-category breakdown and optimization suggestions for context-heavy tools, memory bloat, and capacity warnings. Run /context all to expand the per-item breakdown when the display is collapsed. This is the single most useful command for answering "where did my window go?"

A subagent also has a finite context and supports the same automatic compaction as the main conversation, and its transcript is independent — a subagent that compacts does not disturb your main window, and vice versa. The full mechanics of delegation, isolation, and orchestration — including when delegation pays off and when it does not — are covered in the Claude Code Subagents and Multi-Agent Orchestration Guide. For long-session purposes, the rule of thumb is: if a piece of work will generate a lot of tool output but you only need the conclusion, delegate it. 

Tool results are the fastest-growing category of context (Section 2.1), so disciplining them pays off directly: Read narrowly. Prefer reading the specific region of a large file over the whole file; prefer a targeted search over a broad one. Every line that enters the window stays until it is compacted away. Filter command output before it lands.

The context lifecycle still applies, but the stakes of losing state are higher because no one is watching to catch a bad compaction in real time. Claude Code automatically tracks its own file edits and creates a checkpoint at each user prompt, letting you rewind to a previous state with /rewind (aliases /checkpoint and /undo, or Escape twice on an empty prompt).

content.title: How to Implement Context Compression
content.text:
Key engineering practices Claude Code uses to implement context compression in its /compact command, including structured summary prompts, no-tool constraints, tiered thresholds, separate state preservation, and failure fallback

The general solution is context compaction: compress an overly long conversation history to free up space so you can keep going. Claude Code is a production-grade coding agent, so let's use it as our case study to see what compaction techniques we can learn from. Claude Code has two ways to trigger compaction. One is manual compaction, where you can type the /compact command at any time to trigger it yourself, say when you feel the conversation has gotten too long and you want to consolidate. The other is automatic compaction, where the system runs a compaction pass on its own when the context is about to fill up, freeing space so you can keep chatting. Manual and automatic compaction are triggered at different times, but the underlying mechanism is the same.

How to Use the /compact Command in Claude Code to Prevent Context Rot

Running /compact at 60% context capacity—not 95%—keeps your Claude Code sessions sharp. Learn when and how to compact with specific preservation instructions.

MindStudio Team
How to Use the /compact Command in Claude Code to Prevent Context Rot

Why Your Claude Code Sessions Drift (and How to Stop It)

Long Claude Code sessions have a predictable failure mode. You start sharp — clear context, accurate responses, tight reasoning. Then, somewhere around the two-hour mark, things get fuzzy. Claude starts forgetting earlier decisions. It re-asks questions you already answered. It suggests code that contradicts what it wrote an hour ago.

This is context rot, and it’s not a bug. It’s what happens when an AI’s working memory fills up and the oldest, most foundational information gets compressed or pushed out. 

The /compact command in Claude Code exists specifically to fight this — but most people use it wrong, waiting until the context window is nearly full instead of treating it as a proactive tool.

This guide covers what /compact actually does, when to run it for maximum effect, and how to write preservation instructions that keep your session coherent across compactions.


What Context Rot Actually Looks Like

Context rot shows up in subtle ways before it becomes obvious.

Early signs include Claude giving slightly inconsistent answers to the same question asked at different points in a session. It might reference a file structure that’s been reorganized, or suggest an approach you already ruled out thirty minutes ago.

Later-stage rot is harder to miss. Claude starts producing code that breaks established patterns. It loses track of the overall goal and optimizes for local problems instead.

Worth being exact about where these live, because it changes whether they're available to us.

**All three are Claude Code, not this interface.** `/compact` compresses conversation history into a summary and replaces the long transcript with shorter context; it doesn't reset the project or delete files, and automatic compaction runs when the context is about to fill up. `/context` visualises current usage as a colored grid with a per-category breakdown — that's the real counter. `cc-context-check` is a third-party tool in the same ecosystem.

We're in the Claude app. None of them are reachable from here. So §H.6's entry — *the context estimate triggering §H.10 — judged, no counter exists* — remains accurate **for this session**, and would become measured if the work moved to Claude Code.

**Two things in that material bear directly on §H, and one is a confirmation you should have.**

First, the thresholds. Auto-compaction fires at roughly 95% of the limit, and practitioner guidance puts 85–90% as the recommended threshold, with 95% often too late. §H.10 fixed 90% by its own argument — that every clause of §H.8 costs context, so a session at exhaustion cannot produce a certificate. That reasoning was arrived at independently and lands inside the recommended band. The clause is calibrated.

Second, and this is the sharper one. The standing advice about compaction is that it is still compression, details can be lost, and the mitigation is to make sure important state is in the filesystem before it happens — plans in files, decisions captured in project documentation when they need to persist. That is §H.0 and §H.4 arriving from the tooling side: *a file survives; a context does not, unless it is made into a file.*

So compaction is not an alternative to the handoff protocol — it is the same operator with a weaker guarantee. Compaction re-closes on a **summary** chosen by the outgoing context. §H closes on the **artefacts**. §H.4 already rules between them: *prefer the artefact to the account of the artefact.* A compaction that fires before the register is written loses the finding; the register write is what makes it survivable either way.

Which is what R 1677–1680 just did, and why registering before opening T7 was the right order rather than a cautious one.

If you want a real counter, the move is to run this project in Claude Code — `/context` would replace §H.10's judged estimate with a measured one, and §H.6 would lose its only *judged* row. That's a project-level decision, not one I'd take.

My estimate here stands at roughly **65%**. T7's elaboration is the next bounded step and fits comfortably inside the remaining budget.

**T7 elaborated. The answer is that no cells are cost, and none ever were — the demand was manufactured by the coordinate name.**

Delivered as owed since 1.7.3. Four measurements, in order.

**1 · `mult` is doing four jobs, not two.** R 1665 recorded one name over two quantities. Split by declared language, the store says four:

| | what `mult` holds | population |
|---|---|---|
| index | 2S+1 of the **ground configuration**, from N | total, exact, zero exceptions |
| LS series | 2S+1 of the **series term**, tracking the parent core | 426 rows, values 0–5 |
| jK series | **constant 2** — the Rydberg electron's own spin | **96 rows, all 2** |
| jj + blank term | **0** | **31 jj + 7 LS + 1 unresolved** |

The last two are not multiplicities. jK's leading digit is 2 on **every one of 96 rows**, because a single outer electron is a doublet by construction — a coordinate taking one value across a whole language distinguishes nothing there. And jj terms like `(1/2,1/2)*` have no 2S+1 at all; the 0 is a **null coerced to a number**, which is §2.9's fault in its plainest form, sitting inside the coordinate rather than beside it.

**2 · What the demand looks like if `mult` is left in the key.** 244 of 554 series land on cells the index refuses — 60 distinct cells across 18 elements. That is larger than R 1665's recorded 69 series / 28 cells, because R 1665 counted the LS ones. Restricted to usable δ, 181 of 409 carry a multiplicity the index does not hold at that (Z, charge).

**3 · The decisive test.** Drop `mult` from the measurement's key and ask whether the cells exist:

> **554 of 554 series land on an existing (Z, charge, ℓ) cell. Zero refused.**

And the key is exact without it: **(Z, charge, ℓ, term, parent) is unique across all 554 rows** — no n-range needed, no collisions. Including Ti I's four rows at `2[9/2]*`, which R 1677 found distinguished only by parent.

**4 · So the elaboration is this.** The 60 refused cells were never a cost the index imposed. They are what appears when a **measurement's** property is written into the **index's** key. The series multiplicity is not the index's `mult`; it is a property of the series, and `MEASUREMENTS.tsv` already carries it exactly, in `term` and `parent`, which were there from R 1650. The index's `mult` was asked to receive something it was never defined over, and 60 cells is the size of that mistake, not the size of a gap in Λ_spectra.

M's ruling — **no cells should be cost** — is therefore not a constraint the data strains against. It is satisfied at zero, and the computation shows why: nothing was ever being added, because every cell already exists.

This also disposes of A.cert cleanly. No operation is required at all — not add-a-coordinate (never admitted), not relabel, not refine. `mult = f(N)` stays exactly as it is, total and exceptionless over the ground configuration. What changes is only that the store stops writing into it.

**Two consequences I'd flag rather than act on.** The `mult` column in `MEASUREMENTS.tsv` is now shown to be either redundant (LS, recoverable from `term`) or vacuous (jK) or false (jj's 0). And T9's language cross-tab plus this give the same verdict from two independent routes, satisfying §2.8: **the coupling language decides what a coordinate can mean**, and a name that survives the crossing unchanged has stopped referring.

The board reads: T7 elaborated and awaiting your ruling; T2 awaiting your word in `SPECTRA.md`; T8 the only ungenerated half of the series construction. Register is at 1680 and both gates are green.

Context estimate: roughly **75%**. Enough for the T7 register entries and one more bounded thread, or for a clean close under §H.8. Your call which.

> clause. **A change of practice survives a handoff only if it is REGISTERED.**

did not exist in this project — a fabricated state, before a single file was read. It was retracted
in the same turn. **A session states nothing about the work until it has read `DIGEST.md`.** §2.14
is usually broken by writing before computing; this was the same fault with no computation at all.

- **Outgoing:** The Method 1.8.1 (2026-08-15). **Incoming:** next session, project folder *The Method*.
- **Final bank:** `restore-point-2_11.tar.gz`. Predecessor: `restore-point-2_10.tar.gz`.

- **1677** T9 diagnosed. All three named causes refused. The generator read one language.
- **1678** Both answers were already on record — R 1650 and R 1664. The questions should not have been asked.

- **1682** The cost was manufactured by the coordinate name — 554 of 554 land on existing cells.
- **1683** "No cells should be cost" is satisfied at zero. A.cert is not invoked at all.
- **1684** **T10 opened:** audit 19's uniqueness guard stops at three digits; two entries are duplicated.

Read with `python3 register_gen.py`, `python3 store_gen.py`, `tar tzf … | wc -l`.

|---|---|

**T2 · Which statistic the cell's δ uses. Owner: M — a RECORDING, not a choice.**
Now 430 of 433 on the enlarged sample; the 18 mean-agreements are all series where median and mean
are identical, so they distinguish nothing. **What would settle it:** M's word written into
`SPECTRA.md`'s declaration.

**T5 · The four Gemini items. Owner: M for direction, Claude for tests.** All four tested. Nothing
from Gemini has entered any index. Unchanged this session.

**T6 · The standing store. Owner: M — RULED, and now mechanically complete for VALUES.**
`store_gen.py` is the store's generator and `MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED.tsv` is inside C3. **What remains
is T8's limits, and only that.**

**T7 · Is `mult` the ground state's or the parent's? Owner: M. ELABORATION DELIVERED (R 1681–1683).**
Answer: neither, and the question dissolves. The index's `mult` stays as it is. **What would settle
it:** M's ruling on whether the `mult` COLUMN of `MEASUREMENTS.tsv` is dropped, refused, or left in
place as redundant/vacuous/false by language. That is a store decision touching no coordinate.

**T8 · The 145 voided δ, and the limit assignment. Owner: Claude, on M's direction.**
Now the ONLY ungenerated half of the series construction. R 1650's fallback — *else the first limit
above its top member* — is what R 1664 voided. Where a parent's limit was never published the series
cannot be defected at all: E measuring the world. May want a named bound.

**T9 · The generator's residue. Owner: Claude. CLOSED (R 1677, 1679).** Diagnosed and repaired.
Residue fell from 196 of 554 to 59. The 62 refusals are named and are cases where δ is UNDEFINED.

**T10 · Audit 19's uniqueness guard. Owner: M. NEW (R 1684).** Two entries duplicated (1215, 1476)
inside a range the guard cannot read. The same expression is simultaneously too loose — it produced
a false positive at R 1679 on a wrapped ` 358.` in prose. **What would settle it:** a ruling on
whether to disambiguate at the SOURCE (prose may not begin a line with a bare number) or at the GATE
(read the entry delimiter, not a digit run). **Repair proposed, not applied.**

- **Z = 120** — *chosen*. E = 0 at any cutoff.
- **Tier thresholds** A ≤ 0.05, B ≤ 0.2, C > 0.2 — *chosen*; R 1666 shows they graded the wrong
  quantity on 55% of rows.
- **The asymptotic perspective = the deepest member** — *chosen* definition, not derived.
- **Reduced-mass R_M from standard atomic weights** — *chosen* isotope convention.
- **The parent match is a STRING EQUALITY on the printed parent, decoration retained** — *chosen*,
  per R 1650's "as printed". `2P*<3/2>` and `2P*<1/2>` are different parents under it.
- **The context estimate triggering §H.10** — *judged*. No counter exists in this interface;
  Claude Code's `/context` would make it measured.
- Historical figures quoting **101,328** stand as history (§H.4).

## 6 · What is read and what is not
**Reading is on demand (R 1668), not a queue.** Newly read this session: `store_gen.py` in full,
`roundtrip.py`'s ARTEFACTS table and runner, audit 19 SEQUENCE at source, the register's entry
format at source. Still unread: Part II (Ch. 6–13), Ch. 15–16, Ch. 19, Parts IV–VII incl. Ch. 34
(Löwdin), all appendices, and the bodies of COMPENDIUM, INDICES, PHYSICS and SPECTRA. ~150,000 words.

## 7 · Resumption order
1. `DIGEST.md`, this bridge, then **both gates before touching anything**.
2. **T8** — the limit assignment. It is the only ungenerated half of the series construction, and
   until it closes, `store_gen.py` inherits what R 1664 voided.
3. **T10** — M's ruling on the gate, then the repair. Two duplicate entries stand in the record
   meanwhile, and the guard is blind to every entry after 999.
4. **T2** — write the median into `SPECTRA.md`'s declaration.
5. **T7's remainder** — M's ruling on the `mult` column of the store.
6. `DIGEST.md` extension from this bridge; then board rows 1 and 2.

## 8 · Standing carry-overs
- **`BOARD.md` is stale** — built at R 1614, register now 1684.
- **`COMPENDIUM.md` line 767** quotes 337 / 101,328 in the present tense.
- **`roundtrip.py` still covers no JSON** — the TSV half is discharged (R 1680); JSON is not.
- The **book gap**: the book cites nothing past R 1225; the register is at 1684 — **459 entries**.
- Book PDF render and its prime audit; nuclear corridor; remaining unclosed indexes; board rows 8, 9.
- **Four NIST captures still pending live re-fetch via pasted URLs** — unrelated to the store.
- **Evidence held, not deleted:** `archive_store_gen_v1.py.bak`, `MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED.v1.bak.tsv`,
  `T9-CENSUS.tsv`, `T9-RESIDUE.tsv`, `T9-TERMS.tsv`, `t9_diag.py`, `t9_probe.py`.

content.text:
**Handoff package complete. Four files above — the same four §H.1 requires, all four or none.**

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `restore-point-2_11.tar.gz` | **the work** — 671 files + 12 dirs, sealed after the certificate, bridge and transcripts inside |
| `BRIDGE-1_8_1-to-next.md` | **the state** — R 1677–1684, seven threads with owners, resumption order |
| `DIGEST.md` | **the orientation** — deliberately *not* extended with this session's entries; that is the incoming session's first act, per the R 1669 precedent, and it doubles as proof the new session read the bridge |
| `HANDOFF-PROTOCOL.md` | **§H itself** — clauses H.0–H.11 |

The register travels inside the bank (`REGISTER.md`, `REGISTER-DATA.md`), so §H.1's fourth item is covered without a separate upload.

**To open the new chat, paste this as the first message alongside the four uploads:**

> Prime Handoff Directive — state when the context window reaches 90% capacity and recommend handoff to a new chat.
>
> Prime Zeno Directive — all actions, calculations, tabulations, builds and executes run in zeno segmentation to prevent crashes and timeouts. Order of work: fetch/search → read/encode → analysis/computation → address/close downstream flags → interpretation/conclusion/report. Each step closes fully before the next opens. (It is a closure operator, not a pipeline: closed under the information it has, reopened only by a recorded fact, re-closed by the same operation on the larger input.)
>
> Read `DIGEST.md` first, then `BRIDGE-1_8_1-to-next.md`, then extract the bank and run both gates before touching anything (§H.7). Extend `DIGEST.md` from the bridge as your first registered act. Then T8.

**What the incoming session should find if everything transferred:** gates at 25/25 and 6/6, register rebuilding to 1,479 headings / 1,477 distinct / max 1684 (the 2-heading gap *is* T10 — it should not "fix" it), `MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED.tsv` at 554 rows with 62 named refusals. If any of those numbers differ, that's a finding, not a rounding error.

One asymmetry worth naming: this handoff is the first where the incoming session may hold a substantially larger window than the outgoing one, given your upgrade. The resumption order was written for a constrained session — T8 first, one bounded thread. With more room, T8 plus the T10 repair (once you rule on it) plus the T2 declaration could plausibly close in a single session. The order still holds; the batch size is the new session's judgment call.

This session is complete under §H.8 — certificate exhibited, bank listed, bridge written. Ready when you are.
